title: Microbial-derived bile acid reverses inflammation in IBD via GPBAR1 agonism and RORgammat inverse agonism.
authors: Biagioli, Michele; Di Giorgio, Cristina; Massa, Carmen; Marchiano, Silvia; Bellini, Rachele; Bordoni, Martina; Urbani, Ginevra; Roselli, Rosalinda; Lachi, Ginevra; Morretta, Elva; Piaz, Fabrizio Dal; Charlier, Bruno; Fiorillo, Bianca; Catalanotti, Bruno; Cari, Luigi; Nocentini, Giuseppe; Ricci, Patrizia; Distrutti, Eleonora; Festa, Carmen; Sepe, Valentina; Zampella, Angela; Monti, Maria Chiara; Fiorucci, Stefano
one_liner_zh: 该文研究微生物源胆汁酸通过GPBAR1和RORgammat调节IBD炎症，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The interplay between the dysbiotic microbiota and bile acids is a critical determinant for development of a dysregulated immune system in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Here we have investigated the fecal bile acid metabolome, gut microbiota composition, and immune responses in IBD patients and murine models of colitis and found that IBD associates with an elevated excretion of primary bile acids while secondary, allo- and oxo- bile acids were reduced. These changes correlated with the disease severity, mucosal expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines, and reduced inflow of anti-inflammatory macrophages and Treg in the gut. Analysis of bile acids metabolome in the feces allowed the identification of five bile acids: 3-oxo-DCA, 3-oxo-LCA, allo-LCA, iso-allo-LCA and 3-oxo-UDCA, whose excretion was selectively decreased in IBD patients and diseased mice. By transactivation assay and docking calculations all five bile acids were shown to act as GPBAR1 agonists and RORgammat inverse agonists, skewing Th17/Treg ratio and macrophage polarization toward an M2 phenotype. In a murine model of colitis, administration of 3-oxo-DCA suffices to reverse colitis development and intestinal dysbiosis in a GPBAR1-dependent manner. In vivo administration of 3-oxo-DCA to colitic mice also reverses disease severity and RORgammat activation induced by a RORgammat agonist and IL-23, a Th17 inducing cytokine. These results demonstrated that intestinal excretion of 3-oxoDCA, a dual GPBAR1 agonist and RORgammat inverse agonist, is reduced in IBD and in models of colitis and its restitution protects against colitis development, highlighting a potential role for this agent in IBD management.
abstract_zh: 肠道菌群失调（dysbiotic microbiota）与胆汁酸之间的相互作用是炎症性肠病（IBD）中免疫系统失调发展的关键决定因素。在此，我们研究了IBD患者及结肠炎小鼠模型中的粪便胆汁酸代谢组、肠道菌群组成及免疫反应，发现IBD与初级胆汁酸排泄升高相关，而次级胆汁酸、别胆汁酸（allo-）和氧代胆汁酸（oxo-）则减少。这些变化与疾病严重程度、黏膜促炎细胞因子和趋化因子的表达以及肠道内抗炎巨噬细胞和Treg流入减少相关。粪便胆汁酸代谢组分析鉴定出五种胆汁酸：3-oxo-DCA、3-oxo-LCA、allo-LCA、iso-allo-LCA和3-oxo-UDCA，其在IBD患者和患病小鼠中的排泄选择性降低。通过反式激活实验和对接计算，所有五种胆汁酸均被证明可作为GPBAR1激动剂和RORgammat反向激动剂，使Th17/Treg比值偏向调节并促进巨噬细胞向M2表型极化。在结肠炎小鼠模型中，给予3-oxo-DCA足以以GPBAR1依赖性方式逆转结肠炎发展和肠道菌群失调。对结肠炎小鼠体内给予3-oxo-DCA还可逆转由RORgammat激动剂和IL-23（一种Th17诱导细胞因子）诱导的疾病严重程度和RORgammat激活。这些结果表明，肠道中3-oxo-DCA（一种双重GPBAR1激动剂和RORgammat反向激动剂）的排泄在IBD及结肠炎模型中减少，其恢复可预防结肠炎发展，凸显了该因子在IBD管理中的潜在作用。
